text: 宁可信其有，不可信其无
pinyin: nìng kě xìn qí yǒu, bù kě xìn qí wú
literal: rather · can · believe · it · exists, not · can · believe · it · does not exist
natural: Better to believe it exists than to believe it doesn't

meaning.en: Better to take a possible risk seriously than to dismiss it.
meaning.zh: 对于可能存在的风险，宁愿相信它存在，也不要轻易否定。

examples.zh: 宁可信其有，不可信其无，还是带把伞吧。
examples.en: Better safe than sorry; take an umbrella.

examples.zh: 宁可信其有，不可信其无，安全隐患必须排查。
examples.en: Better to assume it exists than not; safety hazards must be checked.

usage.en: Used for risk, superstition and rumours alike.
usage.zh: 用于风险、迷信或传闻。

text: 有理走遍天下，无理寸步难行
pinyin: yǒu lǐ zǒu biàn tiān xià, wú lǐ cùn bù nán xíng
literal: have · reason · walk · all · under heaven, lack · reason · inch · step · hard · go
natural: With reason you can go anywhere; without it you can't take a step

meaning.en: If you are in the right you can go anywhere; if not, you can't get far.
meaning.zh: 占着道理，到哪里都行得通；没有道理，寸步难行。

examples.zh: 有理走遍天下，无理寸步难行，这件事我们按规矩办。
examples.en: With reason you go anywhere, without it you can't move; let's do this by the rules.

examples.zh: 有理走遍天下，无理寸步难行，别怕，我们有理。
examples.en: Don't worry, we're in the right, and being right gets you anywhere.

usage.en: Used in disputes and consumer-rights contexts.
usage.zh: 多用于争论、维权等场合。

pinyin: yǒu lǐ bú zài shēng gāo
variants: 有理不在声高，无理不怕人多
literal: have · reason · not · lie in · voice · loud
natural: Being right isn't about being loud

meaning.en: Shouting doesn't make you right; reasoned argument does.
meaning.zh: 有道理不必靠大声嚷嚷。

equivalents: The loudest voice isn't always right
Empty vessels make the most sound

examples.zh: 有理不在声高，大家坐下来慢慢说。
examples.en: Being right isn't about volume; let's sit down and talk calmly.

examples.zh: 有理不在声高，吵架解决不了问题。
examples.en: Shouting doesn't make you right, and quarrelling solves nothing.

usage.en: Often contrasted with 无理不怕人多 (no reason, but safe in numbers). Used to calm quarrels.
usage.zh: 常用来劝架、让人冷静。

pinyin: yǒu fú tóng xiǎng, yǒu nàn tóng dāng
literal: have · fortune · together · enjoy, have · trouble · together · bear
natural: Share blessings and bear hardships together

meaning.en: Share both the good times and the bad with each other.
meaning.zh: 好处一起享受，困难一起承担，形容关系亲密。

equivalents: In good times and in bad

examples.zh: 咱们兄弟有福同享，有难同当。
examples.en: We brothers share the good and the bad.

examples.zh: 夫妻就应该有福同享，有难同当。
examples.en: Husbands and wives should share both blessings and hardship.

usage.en: Common in oaths of brotherhood and in wedding or friendship toasts.
usage.zh: 常见于结拜誓言以及婚礼、友情祝词。

pinyin: yǒu chóu bú bào fēi jūn zǐ
variants: 有仇不报非君子，有冤不伸枉为人
literal: have · grudge · not · repay · not · gentleman
natural: A man who doesn't avenge a grudge is no gentleman

meaning.en: A traditional creed that one must take revenge for wrongs done to one.
meaning.zh: 旧时观念：受了仇恨不去报复，就不算大丈夫。

equivalents: Revenge is a dish best served cold

examples.zh: 他嘴上说有仇不报非君子，其实只是想出口气。
examples.en: He says a man who doesn't avenge a grudge is no gentleman, but really he only wants to let off steam.

examples.zh: 有仇不报非君子，这句老话在今天可不能当真。
examples.en: 'No gentleman lets a grudge go' is an old saying we shouldn't take literally today.

usage.en: Often quoted jokingly. The complete saying is 有仇不报非君子，有冤不伸枉为人. Mostly in fiction and martial-arts dramas.
usage.zh: 常半开玩笑地引用，多见于小说和武侠剧。

pinyin: yǒu qián nán mǎi xīn tóu hǎo
literal: have · money · hard · buy · heart's · favourite
natural: Money can't buy what you really love

meaning.en: Money can't always buy something that truly pleases you; people pay what it takes for what they love.
meaning.zh: 钱买不到真正喜欢的东西；心里喜欢的，花多少钱也值得。

equivalents: What the heart wants, the heart wants

examples.zh: 有钱难买心头好，这把琴再贵我也要买。
examples.en: Money can't buy what you love; however expensive, I'm buying this violin.

examples.zh: 有钱难买心头好，我就是喜欢这个老物件。
examples.en: I just love this old piece, and money can't buy that feeling.

usage.en: Often used to justify an indulgent purchase.
usage.zh: 常用来为任性消费找理由。

pinyin: yǒu qián nán mǎi zǎo zhī dào
literal: have · money · hard · buy · early · knowing
natural: Money can't buy advance knowledge

meaning.en: If only I had known earlier; hindsight is something money can't buy.
meaning.zh: 钱买不到事先的预知，感叹事后才明白。

examples.zh: 早知道会涨价就好了，真是有钱难买早知道。
examples.en: If only I'd known the price would rise; money can't buy foresight.

examples.zh: 有钱难买早知道，当初听你的就好了。
examples.en: Hindsight is a luxury; I should have taken your advice.

usage.en: A rueful remark made after a mistake.
usage.zh: 出错之后的懊悔感叹。

text: 没有三两三，不敢上梁山
pinyin: méi yǒu sān liǎng sān, bù gǎn shàng liáng shān
variants: 没有三分三，不敢上梁山
literal: not · have · three · liang · three, not · dare · go up · Liangshan
natural: Without three liang and three, you wouldn't dare go up Liangshan

meaning.en: You need real ability to take on a challenge.
meaning.zh: 没有真本事，就不敢承担重任。

equivalents: You need the right stuff to take on a big challenge

examples.zh: 没有三两三，不敢上梁山，他敢接这个大项目，肯定有把握。
examples.en: Without real ability you wouldn't dare take it on, so he must be confident about this major project.

examples.zh: 没有三两三，不敢上梁山，你别小看他。
examples.en: He wouldn't have dared without real skill; don't underestimate him.

usage.en: Refers to the outlaws of Water Margin joining Liangshan Marsh; 三两三 is a humorous 'some real stuff'.
usage.zh: 借用《水浒传》梁山好汉的典故，“三两三”表示真本事。

text: 没吃过猪肉，也见过猪跑
pinyin: méi chī guo zhū ròu, yě jiàn guo zhū pǎo
literal: not · eaten · pork, also · seen · pig · run
natural: Even if you've never eaten pork, you've seen pigs run

meaning.en: I may not have done it myself, but I know the basics from having seen it.
meaning.zh: 虽然没亲自做过，但也见过别人做，多少有些了解。

equivalents: I may not be an expert, but I've seen it done

examples.zh: 没吃过猪肉，也见过猪跑，这点小事我还是懂的。
examples.en: I haven't done it myself, but I've seen it done; I understand a thing or two.

examples.zh: 没吃过猪肉，也见过猪跑，你别糊弄我。
examples.en: Don't fool me: I may not have tried it, but I've seen it.

usage.en: Self-deprecating or defensive: claim of second-hand knowledge. Casual.
usage.zh: 自谦或为自己辩解，表示有间接经验。口语。

text: 老虎不发威，你当我是病猫
pinyin: lǎo hǔ bù fā wēi, nǐ dàng wǒ shì bìng māo
variants: 老虎不发威，当我是病猫
literal: tiger · not · show · might, you · take · me · as · sick · cat
natural: If the tiger doesn't show its power, you think I'm a sick cat

meaning.en: Don't take my patience for weakness; I can fight back.
meaning.zh: 别把我的忍让当成软弱，我也是有脾气的。

examples.zh: 老虎不发威，你当我是病猫？今天这事必须说清楚！
examples.en: Do you take me for a sick cat just because I haven't roared? We'll settle this today!

examples.zh: 老虎不发威，你当我是病猫，别逼我。
examples.en: Don't mistake my patience for weakness; don't push me.

usage.en: Said angrily or as a playful bluff. 当 here is dàng, 'take as'.
usage.zh: 带怒气或半开玩笑的威胁。“当”读 dàng。

text: 老鼠拉木锨，大头在后头
pinyin: lǎo shǔ lā mù xiān, dà tóu zài hòu tou
variants: 老鼠拖木锨，大头在后头
literal: mouse · drag · wooden shovel, big · end · at · back
natural: A mouse dragging a wooden shovel: the big end is behind

meaning.en: The best part (or the real trouble) is still to come.
meaning.zh: 精彩的、重要的部分（或更大的麻烦）还在后面。

equivalents: The best is yet to come
You haven't seen the half of it

examples.zh: 别高兴太早，老鼠拉木锨，大头在后头呢。
examples.en: Don't celebrate too early; the biggest part is still to come.

examples.zh: 这只是开始，老鼠拉木锨，大头在后头。
examples.en: This is only the start; the big part comes later.

usage.en: A northern rustic saying; can mean good or bad things still to come.
usage.zh: 北方俗语，好事坏事都可以说“还在后头”。

pinyin: sān suì kàn dà, qī suì kàn lǎo
literal: three · years old · see · adult, seven · years old · see · old age
natural: At three you can see the adult; at seven, the old man

meaning.en: A child's character shows what kind of adult they will become.
meaning.zh: 小时候的性格和习惯能看出一个人长大后以至老年的样子。

equivalents: The child is father of the man
As the twig is bent, so grows the tree

examples.zh: 三岁看大，七岁看老，这孩子从小就爱帮忙，长大一定是个热心人。
examples.en: At three you can see the adult; he has always loved helping, so he'll surely be kind-hearted.

examples.zh: 三岁看大，七岁看老，教育要从小抓起。
examples.en: The saying goes that character shows early, so education must start young.

usage.en: A folk belief about early character; use with care since it can be limiting.
usage.zh: 民间关于性格早成的说法，不宜绝对化。

antonyms: 士别三日，即更刮目相待

pinyin: fàng xià tú dāo, lì dì chéng fó
literal: put down · butcher's knife, on the spot · become · Buddha
natural: Put down the butcher's knife and become a Buddha on the spot

meaning.en: A wrongdoer who truly repents can quickly become good.
meaning.zh: 作恶的人只要真心悔改，就能立刻变成好人。

examples.zh: 放下屠刀，立地成佛，只要他真心悔改，社会就应该给他机会。
examples.en: Put down the knife and become a Buddha: if he truly repents, society should give him a chance.

examples.zh: 放下屠刀，立地成佛，何必揪住他的过去不放呢。
examples.en: Why hold on to his past when a repentant person can change at once?

usage.en: Buddhist-flavoured. Sometimes used ironically about someone who has just stopped doing wrong.
usage.zh: 带佛教色彩，有时讽刺刚刚收手的人。

pinyin: fó yào jīn zhuāng, rén yào yī zhuāng
literal: Buddha · needs · gold gilding, person · needs · clothes
natural: A Buddha needs gilding, a person needs clothes

meaning.en: Good clothes improve a person's appearance as gilding does a Buddha statue.
meaning.zh: 佛像要贴金才好看，人要穿得好才显精神。

examples.zh: 佛要金装，人要衣装，去见客户穿得体面点。
examples.en: A Buddha needs gilding and a person needs clothes; dress smartly to meet the client.

examples.zh: 佛要金装，人要衣装，换身衣服就不一样了。
examples.en: A change of clothes makes all the difference.

usage.en: Same idea as 人靠衣装，佛靠金装, with the clauses reversed.
usage.zh: 与“人靠衣装，佛靠金装”意思相同。

pinyin: chū jiā rén bù dǎ kuáng yǔ
literal: left · home · person · not · tell · lies
natural: A monk tells no lies

meaning.en: Monks do not lie; used to vouch that what one says is true.
meaning.zh: 佛教徒不说假话，常借以保证所言属实。

equivalents: Honest as the day is long

examples.zh: 出家人不打诳语，我说的句句是实话。
examples.en: A monk tells no lies, and every word I say is true.

examples.zh: 出家人不打诳语，所以他答应的事一定做到。
examples.en: A monk tells no lies, so what he promises is certain.

usage.en: 诳 (kuáng) means deceptive speech. Often quoted in fiction and opera by monk characters.
usage.zh: 诳指骗人的话。多见于小说、戏曲中僧人所说。

pinyin: pǎo de liǎo hé shang, pǎo bù liǎo miào
literal: run · can · monk, run · cannot · temple
natural: The monk may run away, but the temple can't

meaning.en: You can run away, but your base or responsibilities remain and can be found.
meaning.zh: 人可以逃走，但他的家业、单位跑不掉，总能找到他。

equivalents: You can run but you can't hide

examples.zh: 跑得了和尚，跑不了庙，欠债的人总得回来。
examples.en: The monk can run but the temple can't; a debtor has to come back sometime.

examples.zh: 跑得了和尚，跑不了庙，他的公司还在这儿呢。
examples.en: His company is still here, so he can't escape.

usage.en: Often an implied threat. The 庙 stands for the person's property or workplace.
usage.zh: 常含威胁意味，“庙”指跑不掉的产业或单位。

pinyin: qiú shén bài fó bù rú qiú jǐ
literal: pray to · gods · worship · Buddha · not · as good as · rely on · self
natural: Praying to gods and Buddhas is not as good as relying on yourself

meaning.en: Rely on your own efforts rather than on luck or the gods.
meaning.zh: 与其祈求神佛保佑，不如靠自己努力。

equivalents: God helps those who help themselves
Heaven helps those who help themselves

examples.zh: 求神拜佛不如求己，考试前把书读熟才是正道。
examples.en: Better rely on yourself than pray; studying well before the exam is the right way.

examples.zh: 求神拜佛不如求己，他靠自己的努力赢得了机会。
examples.en: Praying to the gods is no substitute for effort; he earned his chance himself.

usage.en: Also 求人不如求己. Encourages self-reliance.
usage.zh: 相近的有“求人不如求己”，鼓励自立。

pinyin: xìn zé líng, bú xìn zé bù líng
literal: believe · then · works, not · believe · then · doesn't work
natural: It works if you believe, and not if you don't

meaning.en: Belief decides whether something works, often said of superstition or placebo.
meaning.zh: 相信了才会灵验，不信就不灵，多指迷信或心理作用。

examples.zh: 信则灵，不信则不灵，这种保健品全靠心理作用。
examples.en: It works if you believe it; this health supplement relies on psychology.

examples.zh: 他说信则灵，不信则不灵，我就当图个心安。
examples.en: He says it works only if you believe it; I'll treat it as peace of mind.

usage.en: Often a half-sceptical remark about fortune-telling, charms or folk remedies.
usage.zh: 常半信半疑地评说算命、护身符、偏方等。

pinyin: bì mén zào chē, chū mén hé zhé
literal: shut · door · build · cart, go out · door · fit · wheel ruts
natural: Build a cart behind closed doors and it fits the ruts when taken out

meaning.en: Work by established standards, and the product will fit in anywhere.
meaning.zh: 按照统一的规矩做事，结果自然符合实际要求。

equivalents: Follow the rules and you'll fit in

examples.zh: 闭门造车，出门合辙，只要按标准做，产品就能通用。
examples.en: Build by the standard behind closed doors and it fits outside; follow the specification and the product works everywhere.

examples.zh: 这套规范就像闭门造车，出门合辙，各厂家都能照做。
examples.en: The specification works like this: build by it and it fits anywhere.

usage.en: The original saying is positive; the shortened 闭门造车 is now used negatively for working in isolation. Don't confuse the two.
usage.zh: 原句含褒义；今天单说“闭门造车”常指脱离实际，含贬义，二者不同。

pinyin: guān qǐ mén lái zuò huáng dì
literal: shut · up · door · be · emperor
natural: Shut the door and play emperor

meaning.en: To act like a king in a small circle, being arrogant without seeing the wider world.
meaning.zh: 在小圈子里称王称霸，自以为了不起。

equivalents: A big fish in a small pond

examples.zh: 他在家关起门来做皇帝，出了门谁也不理他。
examples.en: He plays emperor at home behind closed doors, but nobody listens outside.

examples.zh: 别关起门来做皇帝了，看看外面的世界吧。
examples.en: Stop playing emperor in your own corner and look at the world outside.

usage.en: Often used of department heads, parents or small-business owners.
usage.zh: 常指小团体的负责人、家长等。

pinyin: guān gōng miàn qián shuǎ dà dāo
literal: Guan Gong · in front of · wield · big · blade
natural: Showing off a sabre in front of Guan Yu

meaning.en: To show off one's skill before a real master.
meaning.zh: 在行家面前卖弄本领，自不量力。

equivalents: Teach your grandmother to suck eggs

examples.zh: 在专业设计师面前谈配色，真是关公面前耍大刀。
examples.en: Discussing colour schemes in front of a professional designer is like showing off a sabre before Guan Yu.

examples.zh: 我这点水平，在你面前不过是关公面前耍大刀。
examples.en: With my modest level, I'm just showing off before a master like you.

usage.en: Often used humbly of oneself. Guan Yu (关公) was famous for his great blade; compare 班门弄斧.
usage.zh: 常作自谦。关羽以大刀闻名，与“班门弄斧”相近。

pinyin: lǔ bān mén qián nòng dà fǔ
literal: Lu Ban · gate · in front of · play with · big · axe
natural: Swinging a big axe at Lu Ban's door

meaning.en: To show off before an expert; to display skill in front of a master.
meaning.zh: 在行家面前显示本领，不自量力。

equivalents: Teach your grandmother to suck eggs

examples.zh: 在老师傅面前讲木工，真是鲁班门前弄大斧。
examples.en: Lecturing an old master on woodwork is swinging an axe at Lu Ban's door.

examples.zh: 我这是鲁班门前弄大斧，让您见笑了。
examples.en: I'm showing off in front of a master; please forgive me.

usage.en: Longer form of 班门弄斧; Lu Ban was the legendary patron of carpenters. Often self-deprecating.
usage.zh: 是“班门弄斧”的长式。鲁班是木匠祖师，常作自谦。

pinyin: qiáng tóu cǎo, suí fēng dǎo
literal: wall · top · grass, follow · wind · fall
natural: Grass on a wall bends with the wind

meaning.en: Someone with no firm views who sides with whoever is stronger.
meaning.zh: 没有主见，哪边势力大就倒向哪边。

equivalents: Trim one's sails to the wind

examples.zh: 他是墙头草，随风倒，谁得势就跟谁。
examples.en: He's grass on the wall bending with the wind, following whoever has power.

examples.zh: 墙头草，随风倒，这样的人不值得信任。
examples.en: Such a fence-sitter who bends with the wind can't be trusted.

usage.en: Often just 墙头草 as a noun for an opportunist.
usage.zh: 常单用“墙头草”指见风使舵的人。
